name: Achan
bio:
Achan was the son of Carmi, great-grandson of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah. After Israel captured Jericho, they turned to attack Ai but were driven back, losing thirty-six men; Joshua fell on his face before the LORD in grief, and the LORD revealed that someone in Israel had secretly kept some of the devoted things, bringing guilt on the whole camp so that it could no longer stand against its enemies (Joshua 7:1-12).

The LORD directed that the guilty party be searched out tribe by tribe, clan by clan, household by household, man by man, and the search finally came to Achan. Joshua said to him, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give him the praise. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me." Achan confessed that among the plunder of Jericho he had seen a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, and coveted and took them, hiding them in the ground inside his tent (Joshua 7:19-21). Joshua sent men to Achan's tent, and there they found everything exactly as described; Achan and all that belonged to him — including his children — were taken to the Valley of Achor, where all Israel stoned them and then burned them, raising a great heap of stones over them, and the LORD's fierce anger was turned away (Joshua 7:22-26).

Achan's story stands as a sobering warning in Scripture against hidden greed and concealed sin that brings disaster not only on oneself but on one's whole household — the very name "Valley of Achor" (meaning "valley of trouble") originates from this episode and is referenced repeatedly in later Scripture.
